durations: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
In a jug, beat the milk, eggs and melted butter together. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined; a few lumps are fine.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe with a little butter.
Pour in about 3 tablespoons of batter per pancake. Cook for 2 minutes until bubbles appear, flip and cook 1 minute more.
Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest. Serve with maple syrup or fruit.
Whisk the eggs, milk, cinnamon and vanilla in a shallow dish.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Dip each slice of bread in the egg mixture for a few seconds per side.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden. Repeat with the remaining bread, adding butter as needed.
Serve hot with maple syrup or fresh fruit.
Beat the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat. Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula.
When the eggs are almost set but still glossy, take off the heat and fold in the cheese.
Spoon onto the toast and scatter with chives.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt half the butter in a frying pan and cook the pepper, green onions and mushrooms for 4 minutes until soft. Tip onto a plate.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan. Cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, season and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Make six wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set.
Heat the oil in a pan and soften the onion and chili for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and beans, season and simmer for 8 minutes.
Melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the pepper for 3 minutes.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the tofu, turmeric and cumin and cook for 4 minutes, stirring.
Heat the oil and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes and oregano. Season, cover partly and simmer for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the cream and season.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water. Add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cook the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet says and drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Top with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs. Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Bring to the boil, then simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until the pasta is cooked and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cook the penne for 2 minutes less than the packet says.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Tip into a baking dish, cover with cheese and bake for 20 minutes.
Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink.
Melt the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook on high until browned.
Add the garlic and paprika for 1 minute, then the stock. Simmer 3 minutes.
Cook the onion, zucchini and eggplant in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes, season and simmer for 10 minutes.
Top with torn mozzarella and parmesan and bake for 40 to 45 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
Roast for 40 minutes until the chicken is golden and cooked through and the potatoes are crisp.
Heat the oil in a wok until very hot. Stir-fry the chicken for 4 minutes and remove.
Stir-fry the vegetables for 3 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken with the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil. Toss for 1 minute and serve with rice.
Heat the oil and cook the onions for 10 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat, then the tomatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and garam masala and simmer 5 minutes more. Season and top with cilantro. Serve with rice or naan.
Brown the chicken in the oil for 5 minutes per side.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until sticky and cooked through.
Cook in a very hot pan for 5 to 6 minutes until cooked, then remove.
Add the rest of the oil and cook the peppers and onion for 5 minutes until charred at the edges.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic.
Pour in the stock, add the thyme and the whole chicken breasts. Simmer for 15 minutes until cooked.
Add the noodles and cook for 5 minutes. Return the chicken, season and add parsley.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and paprika, then stir in the rice.
Pour in the stock, return the chicken, cover and simmer gently for 18 minutes.
Scatter over the peas, cover again for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and season.
Season the chicken and cook in a little oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side. Rest, then slice.
Mix the yogurt, spices, crushed garlic, grated ginger, lemon juice and salt. Stir in the chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Grill or cook in a hot griddle pan for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Brown the beef with the onion in a dry pan for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, spices and tomato paste with a splash of water. Simmer 5 minutes and season.
Soften the onion and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic.
Add the beef and brown well. Stir in the spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste and stock. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the beans and cook 10 minutes more. Season and serve with rice.
Cook in a hot pan or grill for 4 to 5 minutes per side. Add the cheese for the last minute.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Stir-fry the beef in very hot oil for 2 minutes and remove.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the broccoli, beef, the rest of the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and 4 tablespoons water. Toss until glossy and serve with rice.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cook the onion and carrot in the oil for 8 minutes, then brown the lamb.
Stir in the tomato paste, worcestershire sauce and stock. Simmer for 15 minutes and add the peas.
Stir the flour into the pan for 1 minute, then whisk in the stock, cream and soy sauce.
Return the meatballs and simmer for 10 minutes until cooked and the sauce has thickened. Serve with mashed potatoes.
Boil the potatoes for 6 minutes and drain well.
Fry them in the oil until golden and crisp, about 10 minutes. Season and keep warm.
Season the steaks and sear in a very hot pan for 2 to 4 minutes per side.
Add the butter, crushed garlic and rosemary and spoon over the steaks. Rest 5 minutes, then serve with the potatoes.
Season the chops and brown in the oil for 4 minutes per side. Remove.
Add the butter, onion and apples and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir in the stock, mustard and thyme, return the chops and simmer for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Cook the onion for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the tomatoes, beans and thyme, return the sausages and simmer for 25 minutes. Season and serve with bread or mash.
Put the onion in a casserole, sit the pork on top and add 150 ml water. Cover and cook for 4 hours until very tender.
Season and bake for 12 to 15 minutes until just flaking. Serve with lemon wedges.
Sear the salmon skin side down in the oil for 4 minutes, then turn.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, spooning it over until glossy.
Fry in the oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side until it flakes.
Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and chili and cook for 2 minutes per side until pink.
Boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash. Poach the fish in simmering water for 5 minutes and flake.
Fry in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden.
Cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, tomatoes and coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes.
Simmer the lentils with the water and turmeric for 20 minutes until soft, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile fry the onion in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and chili for 1 minute, then the tomatoes for 3 minutes.
Stir the onion mixture into the lentils, season and simmer 5 minutes. Top with cilantro.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the carrot for 2 minutes, then the peas, garlic and most of the green onions.
Add the rice and stir-fry for 4 minutes until hot.
Shape into four patties and chill for 10 minutes if you have time.
Fry in the oil for 5 to 6 minutes per side until crisp.
Cook the onion in the oil and half the butter for 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and garlic and cook until browned.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, letting each addition absorb before the next. This takes about 20 minutes.
When the rice is creamy and just tender, stir in the remaining butter and parmesan. Season and rest 2 minutes.
Stir-fry the vegetables in the hot oil for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the noodles, soy sauce and honey. Toss for 2 minutes and serve.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Line a 23 cm tart tin with the pastry and bake blind for 12 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, milk, nutmeg, salt and pepper and pour over. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until just set.
Bake on trays for 8 to 10 minutes until crisp and bubbling. Scatter with basil.
Soften the onion, peppers and sweet potato in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and 200 ml water. Simmer for 25 minutes until the sweet potato is tender.
Fill the pepper halves, place in a dish and cover with foil. Bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover, top with cheese and bake 10 minutes more.
Heat the grill (broiler). Cook the onion, zucchini and pepper in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 8 minutes. Add the spinach to wilt.
Cook on low for 8 minutes until the base is set.
Scatter over the rest of the cheese and grill for 3 to 4 minutes until puffed and golden.
Fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side until crisp.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Toss the sweet potato with the oil, spices and salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Brush the eggplant slices with oil, season and roast on trays for 20 minutes.
Simmer the garlic and tomatoes with the oregano for 10 minutes. Season.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling. Scatter with basil.
Stir-fry the sliced pepper and broccoli for 4 minutes.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, tomatoes and 250 ml water. Cover and simmer for 18 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the peas for 3 minutes, season and scatter with cilantro.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan for 2 to 3 minutes per side until crisp and melted. Cut into wedges.
Cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the eggplant and cook 5 minutes, then the zucchini, peppers and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and thyme, cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Boil the cauliflower for 5 minutes and drain well.
Mix with the cauliflower in a dish, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 20 minutes.
Cook the onion in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes.
Dice the onion, carrot and celery and cook in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beans and pasta and cook for 10 minutes, adding the shredded kale for the last 3.
Melt the butter and cook the leeks gently for 8 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer for 15 minutes until soft.
Chop the vegetables and cook in the oil for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Cook the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the squash and spices and cook 3 minutes.
Add the stock and simmer for 20 minutes until the squash is soft.
Melt the butter and cook the onions with the sugar very slowly for 40 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
Stir in the flour, then add the stock and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes. Season.
Cook the chopped onion and pepper in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin.
Add the beans and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Bring the stock to a simmer with the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tofu and spinach for 1 minute. Take off the heat and stir in the miso and soy sauce.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Chop the vegetables, toss with 1 tablespoon oil and roast for 25 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer in 400 ml water for 15 minutes. Drain and cool slightly.
Toss everything with the oil, lemon juice, cumin and salt. Rest 10 minutes for the flavors to mingle.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes, adding the green beans for the last 4. Drain and cool.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and halve.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Peel and chop the potatoes and boil in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until very tender.
Drain well and let steam for 2 minutes.
Toss the broccoli with the oil, sliced garlic and salt and roast for 18 to 20 minutes until charred at the edges.
Toss with melted butter, honey, thyme and salt and roast for 25 minutes until tender and glazed.
Put everything in a saucepan, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Boil the beans for 3 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then toss in the beans for 2 minutes. Season and scatter with toasted almonds.
Cook the chopped onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and stock, cover and simmer gently for 18 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Season.
Wrap in foil and bake for 10 minutes, then open the foil for 2 minutes to crisp.
Cook in a pan over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and melted.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking halfway, until crunchy. They crisp more as they cool.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until melted.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool before slicing.
Roll into 16 balls, space well apart and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool on the tray.
Scatter over the apples and bake for 35 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Microwave on high for 60 to 90 seconds until risen but still slightly gooey. Cool for a minute.
Cook on low for 35 to 40 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Scatter with berries and chopped almonds. Freeze for 3 hours, then break into pieces.
Chill for 20 minutes, then roll into about 18 balls. Keep in the fridge.
Fold in the flour and milk. Divide between the cases and bake for 18 to 20 minutes. Cool.
Fill the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden.
Spoon into small glasses and chill for 30 minutes. Top with berries if you like.
Add a splash of water to the dish and bake for 30 minutes until tender.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt to a smooth thin batter. Rest for 10 minutes if you can.
Cook for 1 minute until set, flip and cook 30 seconds.
Stir-fry the garlic and shrimp in the oil for 2 minutes. Push aside, scramble the eggs in the space.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes. Add the bean sprouts and green onions.
Cook the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste.
Return the beef, add the stock, bay leaves and thyme. Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes in chunks and cook 45 minutes more, until the beef is tender. Season.
Cook the sliced onion in the oil for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 5 to 6 minutes until it flakes.
Cook the chopped onion for 5 minutes, add the garlic and oregano, then the orzo for 1 minute.
Add the stock, return the chicken and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until the orzo is tender.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and chili. Cook 2 minutes until glossy.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prick the potatoes, rub with a little oil and salt and bake for 1 hour until crisp outside and soft inside.
Meanwhile cook the chopped onion in the rest of the oil for 6 minutes. Add the spices, beans and tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir-fry the cabbage and green onions in the rest of the oil for 2 minutes. Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss.
Put the tomatoes, olives and sliced garlic in a baking dish with the oil, toss and roast for 8 minutes.
Nestle in the fish, season, add lemon slices and bake 12 minutes more until the fish flakes.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the bok choy cut side down and cook for 2 minutes, then turn and add 2 tablespoons of water. Cover for 2 minutes until the stems are just tender.
Fry the tempeh in the oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side until golden. Pour in the sauce and let it bubble and coat the tempeh, about 1 minute.
Toss the chickpeas, peppers, onion and zucchini with the olive oil, paprika, cumin and a pinch of salt on a large tray. Roast for 20 minutes.
Add the halloumi, stir and roast for 10 minutes more until the cheese is golden at the edges.
Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Add the pork and cook, breaking it up, for 6-8 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then stir in the sauce and cook for 2 minutes until sticky.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes per side until crisp and the cheese melts.
Fry the mushrooms in the oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add the noodles and spinach and simmer for 2-3 minutes until hot and wilted.
Fry the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and spices and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and coconut milk. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until tall and golden.
Cook until bubbles form and the edges look set, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Cook spoonfuls of batter in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Pour enough batter to cover the iron plates, close and cook for 4-5 minutes until crisp and golden.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until puffed and set in the middle. Cool for 5 minutes before lifting out.
Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain well.
Brown the sausage meat in the oil in a large frying pan, breaking it up, for 5 minutes. Add the onion, pepper and potatoes.
Season with paprika and salt and fry for 12-15 minutes, turning now and then, until the potatoes are crisp.
Make four hollows, crack in the eggs, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes until the whites are set.
Heat the oil in a large pan, pour in the sauce and simmer for 8 minutes until slightly thickened. Season with salt.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar. Poach the eggs, a few at a time, for 3 minutes.
Toast in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes per side until crisp and the cheese melts.
Pour into the dish, scatter with walnuts and bake for 35 minutes until golden and just set.
Brush with egg, top with the rest of the cheese and bake for 15-18 minutes until risen and golden.
Lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for about 1 hour, stirring every 10 minutes, until thick and creamy. Add water if it gets too thick.
Roll again and repeat until the egg is used. Rest for 2 minutes, then slice.
Cook for 2 minutes until almost set, then fold and cook 30 seconds more. Repeat to make four omelettes.
Rinse the poha in a sieve under cold water for 30 seconds, then leave to drain and soften.
Add the onion and chili and cook 4 minutes, then the turmeric and peas for 2 minutes.
Fold in the poha with the sugar and a good pinch of salt, cover for 2 minutes on low heat, then squeeze over the lemon.
Add the rice and peas and stir-fry over high heat for 4-5 minutes until hot and starting to crisp.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and add the sweet potato. Cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the onion, pepper, paprika, cumin and a pinch of salt and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the potato is crisp at the edges.
Stir in the black beans to warm through for 3 minutes. Top with avocado.
Leave for 10 minutes, whisk again to break up any clumps, then cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Spread out on the tray and bake for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden.
Fry in batches in the butter over medium heat for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Melt the butter in a large pan over high heat, add the mushrooms and cook without stirring for 3 minutes until browned.
Add the garlic and thyme, season with salt and pepper and cook 3 minutes more.
Fry the onion and jalapeno in the oil for 3 minutes, then add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard and a pinch of salt and pour over. Press the bread down and leave for 15 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Scatter over the rest of the cheese and bake for 40-45 minutes until puffed and set.
Bring the milk and a pinch of salt to a simmer and whisk in the polenta. Cook, stirring, for 5-8 minutes until thick, then stir in the butter and parmesan.
Fry the tomatoes in the oil for 3 minutes, push aside and fry the eggs.
Simmer the quinoa with the almond milk, water and cinnamon for 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until creamy and tender.
Bake for 18-20 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Squeeze over lemon, dust with powdered sugar and serve at once.
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beans with about 4 tablespoons of their liquid and simmer for 3 minutes.
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes, habanero and thyme for 3 minutes.
Add the fish and cook 2 minutes, then pour in the beaten eggs and stir gently until just set.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, add the garlic, chili flakes and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes until the paste darkens.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 8 minutes, then stir in the cream.
Toast the pepper in a large pan for 1 minute, add the butter and 150 ml pasta water and bring to a simmer.
Add the pasta, take the pan off the heat and wait 30 seconds, then add the cheese a handful at a time, tossing hard and adding water until creamy.
Fry the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, rosemary and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and stock, simmer for 10 minutes, then mash about a third of the chickpeas against the pan.
Add the pasta and cook, stirring often, until tender and the soup is thick, about 10 minutes. Remove the rosemary and serve with parmesan.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Cook the pasta; add the broccoli for the last 4 minutes. Save a mug of water and drain.
Brown the sausage in the oil, breaking it up, for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Brown the mushrooms in the butter over high heat for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Pour in the cream and simmer 2 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cook the pasta for 2 minutes less than the packet says and drain.
Brown the beef with the onion for 8 minutes, then add the marinara and oregano and simmer 5 minutes.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until bubbling and browned.
Cook the pasta, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes. Save a mug of water.
Fry the zucchini, pepper and asparagus in the oil over medium-high heat for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and capers and simmer 10 minutes.
Fry the sage leaves in the butter until crisp, lift out, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the pumpkin, stock and nutmeg and simmer 3 minutes. Toss with the pasta and parmesan and top with the crispy sage.
Brown the chicken in the butter for 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Simmer, stirring often, for 12-14 minutes until the pasta is tender and the sauce coats it. Stir in the parmesan and parsley.
Fry the garlic in the oil for 30 seconds, add the orzo and stir 1 minute.
Add the stock and simmer, stirring often, for 10-12 minutes until the orzo is tender and creamy.
Stir-fry the carrots and mushrooms in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes, add the snow peas, garlic and green onions for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes until hot.
Fry the pork in the oil until browned and crispy, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and cook 1 minute.
Loosen the udon in hot water for 1 minute and drain.
Fry the pork in the oil until golden, then add the onion, carrot and cabbage and stir-fry 4 minutes.
Add the noodles with the soy sauce, mirin and Worcestershire sauce and toss over high heat for 2-3 minutes.
Cook the soba with the edamame for 4-5 minutes, then rinse under cold water until cool and drain.
Stir-fry the chicken in the oil over high heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, chilies and pepper for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar and toss for 2 minutes. Stir in the basil until wilted.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, squeeze dry and chop.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot and mushrooms in the vegetable oil for 4 minutes, adding the garlic at the end.
Scramble the eggs in a little oil, then set aside. Stir-fry the shrimp in the rest of the oil for 2 minutes.
Add the pepper and curry powder for 1 minute, then the noodles, soy sauce and a splash of water. Toss until evenly yellow.
Melt the butter and cook the garlic gently for 2 minutes without browning.
Simmer the stock with the ginger and garlic, add the chicken and poach gently for 15 minutes. Lift out and slice.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Stir-fry the chicken and garlic in the oil over high heat for 4 minutes, then add the broccolini for 2 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs, then add the noodles and sauces. Toss and let the noodles char a little, about 3 minutes.
Add the tortellini and simmer following the packet, about 3-4 minutes.
Melt the butter with the sage over medium heat until nutty and golden, about 3 minutes.
Add the gnocchi and toss for 2 minutes so they color slightly. Finish with parmesan, lemon and black pepper.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway, until the gnocchi are golden and the sausage is cooked. Top with parmesan.
Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Cook the pasta 2 minutes under the packet time and drain.
Top with mozzarella and parmesan and bake for 25-30 minutes until bubbling.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute. Whisk in the milk and simmer 3 minutes until thick.
Warm the oil with the garlic and chili, add the clams and wine, cover and cook for 4-5 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay closed.
Add the pasta and a splash of its water to the clams and toss for 1 minute. Finish with parsley.
Sear the beef in half the butter over high heat for 1-2 minutes, in batches, and set aside.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the rest of the butter for 8 minutes. Sprinkle in the flour, then stir in the stock and simmer 3 minutes.
Brown the beef in a large pan for 6 minutes and drain off excess fat. Stir in the taco seasoning.
Add the tomatoes, stock and macaroni, bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 10-12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in most of the cheese, top with the rest and the green onions, and cover for a minute to melt.
Mix the chicken with the yogurt, ginger garlic paste, spices and 1 teaspoon of salt. Leave for 20 minutes or longer.
Fry the onions in the ghee for 12 minutes until deep golden. Remove half for the top.
Parboil the rice in salted water for 5 minutes and drain.

Add the chicken to the pot with the remaining onions and cook 10 minutes. Layer the rice over, drizzle with the saffron milk, scatter with mint and fried onion. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 minutes until just tender; drain.
Fry the onions slowly in the oil for 25-30 minutes until deep brown and some are crisp. Lift out half.
Add the rice, cumin and cinnamon to the pan and stir 1 minute, then add the lentils, 500 ml water and 1 teaspoon salt.
Cover and cook on low for 18 minutes, then rest 5 minutes. Serve topped with the reserved onions and yogurt.
Slice the other onion and fry in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomato paste and fry 3 minutes, then add the blended sauce, curry powder, thyme and bay leaves. Simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Stir in the rinsed rice and stock, season with salt, cover tightly and cook on low for 25-30 minutes, without stirring, until the rice is tender.
Season the chicken with salt, cumin and paprika and brown in the oil for 4 minutes per side. Set aside.
Fry the onion, pepper and garlic for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, saffron and rice.
Add the stock, nestle the chicken back in, cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes.
Scatter over the peas, cover again for 5 minutes and serve.
Fry the bacon until crisp, add the kimchi and fry 3 minutes.
Add the rice, gochujang, kimchi juice and soy sauce and stir-fry for 5 minutes until hot and a little crispy.
Fry the rice in the oil over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until lightly golden.
Add the onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, cumin and stock with a pinch of salt.
Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Cover and cook on low for 15-18 minutes until the water is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes.
Simmer the quinoa in the stock, covered, for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Rest 5 minutes.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the butter for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and thyme.
Stir in the barley, then add the stock a ladleful at a time over 40 minutes, stirring often, until tender and creamy.
Soften the onion in the oil and half the butter for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir 1 minute.
Add the wine and let it bubble away, then add the stock a ladleful at a time, stirring, for about 18 minutes.
Cook the squash and onion in the oil for 10 minutes until the squash starts to soften.

Marinate the chicken in the gochujang, gochugaru, soy, sugar and garlic for 30 minutes.
Stir-fry the sweet potato and onion in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, cabbage and rice cakes and cook 12 to 15 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir-fry the shrimp and sausage in a smoking wok for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss 2 minutes, push aside and scramble the eggs into the noodles.
Add the bean sprouts and chives and toss 30 seconds.
Marinate the fish in the turmeric, fish sauce, sugar and ginger for 20 minutes.
Pan-fry in the oil over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Marinate the chops in the fish sauce, sugar, garlic, lemongrass and oil for at least 1 hour.
Grill or pan-fry 3 to 4 minutes per side until caramelised.
Add the chicken, the rest of the coconut milk and the stock and simmer 20 minutes; season with fish sauce and sugar.
Fry the curry paste in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the beans, fish sauce, sugar and a splash of water and cook 3 minutes.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, add the onions and cook 10 minutes until brown.
Add the chickpeas and 300 ml water and simmer 20 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Cook the onions, tomatoes and paste in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes, blend with the soaked cashews and return to the pan with the spices and 200 ml water.
Simmer 10 minutes, stir in the cream and add the kofta just before serving.
Stir-fry the peppers and onion in the oil for 3 minutes and set aside.
Cook the paste and tomatoes with the ground spices until thick, add the paneer, vegetables, garam masala and methi and toss for 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste, then the wine and vinegar and bubble 2 minutes.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, spices and enough water to cover and simmer covered for 1 1/2 to 2 hours until very tender.
Cook the onion and zucchini in half the oil, add the rice, tomato flesh, herbs and salt and simmer 5 minutes.
Drizzle with the rest of the oil and 200 ml water and bake at 190 °C (375 °F) for 60 to 70 minutes.
Rub the lamb with crushed garlic, lemon, oregano, oil and salt and marinate at least 2 hours.
Bake at 160 °C (325 °F) for 4 hours until falling apart, then open and brown at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Return the shanks, cover and simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours until tender.
Bring the stock to a simmer, drop in the meatballs and cook 10 minutes.
Add the hot stock, saffron and noodles, spread evenly and simmer 10 minutes.
Push in the shrimp and cook 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed; serve with lemon and aioli.
Cook the onion and peppers in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the eggplant and zucchini and cook 10 minutes more.
Add the garlic and tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes until thick.
Add the saffron and paprika and simmer very gently for 2 to 2 1/2 hours, adding cold water occasionally so the beans stay covered.
Poach the cod 5 minutes, then flake, removing skin and bones.
Simmer covered for 1 1/2 hours, add the kielbasa and cook 30 minutes more; it tastes better the next day.
Pour over the tomato sauce, cover and bake at 175 °C (350 °F) for 1 1/2 hours.
Knead the flour, egg, water and salt to a firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Boil in salted water for 6 to 8 minutes after they float; toss with butter and serve with sour cream and dill.
Beat the flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg and salt to a thick sticky batter and rest 10 minutes.
Layer the spaetzle and cheese in a dish, top with the onions and bake at 200 °C (400 °F) for 10 minutes; scatter with chives.
Brown in the oil, add the stock and wine, cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours until tender.
Knead the flour, water, oil and salt to a smooth dough and rest 20 minutes.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes until crisp and blistered.
Rub the butter into the flour and salt, add the water and bring together; chill 30 minutes.
Brush with egg and bake at 200 °C (400 °F) for 20 minutes, then at 170 °C (340 °F) for 30 minutes.
Cook the oil and flour over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 25 to 30 minutes to a dark brown roux.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook 8 minutes, then the garlic.
Whisk in the stock, add the chicken, sausage, seasoning and bay and simmer 1 hour.
Cook the butter and flour, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes to a peanut-coloured roux.
Add the vegetables and cook 8 minutes, then the garlic and seasoning.
Stir in the stock and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the crawfish and cook 5 minutes; serve over rice with green onions.
Fry at 160 °C (325 °F) for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until golden and the inside reads 74 °C (165 °F).
Stir in the macaroni, cover and simmer 12 minutes, stirring, until tender.
Simmer everything except the corn and beans in a large pot for 40 minutes.
Add the corn and beans and simmer 20 minutes more until thick.
Simmer covered for 2 1/2 to 3 hours until falling from the bone, adding the beans for the last 20 minutes.
Cover and cook on low for 30 to 35 minutes until the rice is tender; remove the pepper and add the cilantro.
Fry the plantain chunks at 175 °C for 8 to 10 minutes until tender and golden.
Roast covered at 160 °C (325 °F) for 4 hours, then uncover and roast at 220 °C (425 °F) for 30 to 45 minutes until the skin crackles.
Simmer the pork in the marinade with water to cover for 1 hour until tender and the liquid has reduced.
Drain and fry in hot oil for 4 to 5 minutes until crisp and browned.
Stir-fry the garlic and shallots in the oil, add the chicken and shrimp and cook 3 minutes.
Push aside, scramble the eggs, then add the cabbage, noodles, kecap manis, soy and sambal and toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Simmer the pork in water with the onion, garlic, ginger, doenjang and coffee for 60 to 70 minutes until tender.
Brown the beef in 2 tbsp oil, add half the onions, the garlic, tomatoes, curry powder and water to cover and simmer 1 hour.
Add the carrots and cook 15 minutes.
Fry the rest of the onion in the remaining oil, add the greens and a splash of water and cook 5 minutes.
Pour into the simmering stock while stirring gently so it forms soft strands; cook 1 minute and add parsley.
Simmer the lamb, barley and peas in the water for 1 hour, skimming.
Add the vegetables and simmer 40 minutes more.
Simmer the chicken in the stock with the cilantro stems for 30 minutes, then shred it.
Add the potatoes and corn and simmer 30 minutes so some potatoes break down to thicken.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer 20 minutes, mashing some to thicken.
Brown the chicken in the oil, add the onion, garlic and aji and cook 5 minutes.
Add the stock, rice and potatoes and simmer 25 minutes.
Add the cilantro puree, pepper and peas and cook 5 minutes; serve with lime.
Simmer the drained beans in fresh water for 30 minutes and drain.
Add the beans, bay, oregano and water to cover by 3 cm and simmer 1 hour until creamy.
Add the potato and onion and simmer 8 minutes.
Add the zucchini, mushrooms, garlic and tofu and simmer 6 minutes.
Simmer the tomatoes, tamarind, pepper, cumin, garlic, turmeric, rasam powder, salt and water for 15 minutes.
Add the greens, okra, coconut milk, stock, thyme and whole pepper and simmer 25 minutes.
Soak the rice cakes in water for 20 minutes.
Brown the beef in the sesame oil with the garlic, add the stock and soy sauce and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the rice cakes and cook 5 minutes until soft and floating.
Stir in the paprika and pour in the stock; simmer 10 minutes.
Crack in the eggs and poach 3 to 4 minutes.
Blend in the oil slowly to a thick, creamy soup and chill 2 hours.
Add the carrots and stock and simmer 25 minutes until very soft.
Mix the matzo meal, eggs, fat, 3 tbsp stock and salt and chill 30 minutes.
Roll into 12 balls with wet hands and simmer in salted water, covered, for 30 to 40 minutes.
Simmer the carrots and celery in the stock for 15 minutes, add the chicken and matzo balls and finish with dill.
Soften the fennel, onion and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, saffron, orange peel and stock and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the fish and shrimp and poach gently 5 minutes.
Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric and nuts to a paste and fry in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, lemongrass, lime leaves, water and salt and simmer 40 minutes.
Steep the tea in the boiling water for 5 minutes, remove and cool.
Chill 2 hours, strain and serve over ice.
Simmer the ginger, sugar and water for 10 minutes and steep until cool.
Steep at least 4 hours or overnight.
Simmer the water with the sugar, cinnamon, orange peel and cloves for 5 minutes.
Stir in the coffee, turn off the heat and steep 5 minutes.
Simmer the water with the spices for 5 minutes.
Add the tea and milk and heat to steaming for 3 minutes.
Cook the tapioca pearls following the packet, about 15 minutes, and drain.
Pat the steaks dry and salt them on both sides 30 minutes ahead if you can.
Heat a heavy pan until very hot. Sear the steaks 3-4 minutes per side.
Add the butter, tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for a minute. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Cook skin side down in a hot pan with a little of the butter for 5-6 minutes until the skin is crisp, then turn for 1-2 minutes.
Cook in a hot pan or on a grill 3-4 minutes per side. Add the cheese for the last minute if using.
Roast at 150 °C for 2 hours, then turn the oven up to 230 °C for 20-30 minutes until the crackling puffs.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut into thick slices.
Roast the bones at 220 °C for 40 minutes until browned.
Put them in a large pot with the water, bring to a bare simmer and skim. Simmer gently, partly covered, for 6-8 hours, topping up with water.
Start skin side down in a cold heavy pan, then cook over medium heat for 20-25 minutes until the fat has rendered and the skin is deep golden.
Turn, add the butter and baste; cook 8-10 minutes more, until 75 °C inside.
Salt the chops and sear in a hot pan 3 minutes per side for pink, holding them fat edge down for a minute to crisp the fat.
Soften the onion and pepper in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, cumin and oregano for a minute.
Add the beans with their liquid and the bay leaf. Simmer 15-20 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken.
Boil the plantains in salted water for 15-20 minutes until very tender.
Meanwhile soften the onion in a little oil, add the vinegar and a pinch of salt and cook 2 minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic in the oil until soft, add the curry powder and cumin with a splash of water and cook 2 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, potato, water and green seasoning. Simmer 15-20 minutes until the potato is soft and the sauce thick; crush some chickpeas.
Simmer the okra in the water with the salt for 8 minutes.
Stir with a wooden spoon for 8-10 minutes until thick and pulling from the sides. Beat in the butter, shape in a buttered bowl and turn out. Serve with flying fish or any stewed fish.
Fry spoonfuls in oil at 175 °C for 3-4 minutes until golden. Drain and serve with a lime and hot sauce dip.
Brown the beef in the oil in batches. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes.

Add the spices, pepper, sugar, cassareep or molasses, thyme and water to just cover. Simmer covered for 2-2½ hours until very tender and the sauce is dark and glossy. Remove the whole pepper. Best the next day.
Cover and simmer gently 40 minutes without stirring, until the breadfruit is tender and has soaked up most of the liquid.
Lay the callaloo on top for the last 10 minutes. Serve from the pot.
Salt the steak and set it on a rack over a tray. Bake at 120 °C until the centre reaches 50 °C, about 45-50 minutes.
Heat the tallow in a heavy pan until smoking and sear the steak 60-90 seconds per side, edges too.
Rest 5 minutes, slice across the grain and season with the pepper.
Heat half the tallow in a wide pan until very hot. Fry half the strips in one layer for 1-2 minutes without moving, then turn for 30 seconds.
Cook in a hot pan 4 minutes per side. Move to bowls.
Return all the ribs, pour in the broth, cover and cook at 150 °C for 3-3½ hours until the meat pulls from the bone.
Rub the brisket all over with the salt and pepper. Leave 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.
Set fat side up in a roasting tin, add the stock, cover tightly with foil and roast at 140 °C for 5 hours until a skewer slides in easily.
Rest 30 minutes in the foil, then slice across the grain and spoon over the juices.
Add the broth, lock the lid and cook at high pressure for 70 minutes. Let the pressure release naturally for 15 minutes.
Shape 4 patties and chill for 15 minutes.
Cook in a hot dry pan 3-4 minutes per side; the marrow bastes the burgers as they cook.
Stand them marrow side up on a tray and roast at 220 °C for 15-20 minutes until the marrow is soft and just starting to pull away.
Melt the butter in a large pan until foaming. Fry the liver 1-2 minutes per side so it stays pink in the middle.
Trim the livers. Fry them in 2 tablespoons of the butter over medium heat for 4-5 minutes until just pink inside.
Pack into a dish, smooth the top and chill for at least 3 hours.
Fry in the foaming butter over high heat for 2 minutes per side.
Grill over very high heat for 2-3 minutes per side, keeping the centre pink.
Cover the tongue with water, add the salt and simmer gently for 3½-4 hours until tender.
Spread on a tray and roast at 200 °C for 45-60 minutes, turning once, until crisp and well browned.
Melt the lard in a heavy pot, add the pork and just enough water to come halfway up. Simmer uncovered for 2½ hours, stirring now and then.
Salt the chops and leave 20 minutes.
Sear in a hot pan with a little butter for 4-5 minutes per side to 63 °C.
Roast at 160 °C for 3½ hours, then turn up to 230 °C for 25 minutes until the skin crackles.
Rest 20 minutes before pulling or carving. Finish with the black pepper.
Wrap in foil and bake at 150 °C for 2 hours.
Unwrap, turn the oven to 220 °C and roast 20-30 minutes until the outside is crusty.
Cover and cook over low heat for 3-4 minutes until the whites are set.
Add the stock, cover and cook gently on the hob or at 150 °C for 2-2½ hours until spoon-tender.
Rub the lamb with the ghee, salt and pepper. Leave at room temperature for 1 hour.
Roast at 220 °C for 20 minutes, then at 180 °C for about 1 hour 10 minutes for pink meat (60 °C in the thickest part).
Rest 20 minutes covered loosely with foil, then carve.
Salt the chops. Stand them on their fatty edge in a cold heavy pan and turn on the heat; render the fat for 4-5 minutes.
Lay the chops flat and cook 3 minutes per side in the rendered fat.
Rest 3 minutes before eating. Finish with the black pepper.
Cover tightly and roast at 150 °C for 4 hours until it falls apart.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes at 200 °C to brown. Pull apart and spoon over the juices.
Knead the lamb with the salt and pepper for 2 minutes until sticky.
Shape into 12 long koftas, on skewers if you like. Chill 20 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry over high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning, until browned and just cooked through.
Add the broth and salt, bring to a bare simmer and cook covered for 2-2½ hours until tender.
Put skin side down in a cold pan and cook over medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, pouring off the fat now and then, until the skin is thin and crisp.
Turn and cook 2 minutes. Rest 5 minutes and slice. Keep the fat for other cooking. Finish with the black pepper.
Roast at 200 °C for 1 hour 10-20 minutes until the juices at the thigh run clear (74 °C).
Rest 15 minutes and carve. Spoon the pan fat over.
Add the chicken, cover and poach very gently, turning once, for 15-20 minutes until it reaches 70 °C.
Rest 5 minutes and slice; spoon over the butter.
Spread on a rack over a tray and roast at 220 °C for 40-45 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Grill over high heat 10-12 minutes, turning often, until the skin is crisp and the meat is cooked through. Finish with the black pepper.
Grill over high heat for 6-8 minutes, turning, until browned outside.
Roast at 190 °C for 1¼-1½ hours until the meat reaches 80 °C near the bone.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice off the bone.
Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 10-12 minutes until cooked through.
Simmer very gently, partly covered, for 6 hours.
Roast the bones at 220 °C for 30 minutes.
Simmer in the water for 6 hours, skimming now and then.
Leave 30 seconds, then stir gently once so the egg forms ribbons.
Cut the belly into strips and salt them. Leave 15 minutes and pat dry.
Cook skin side down in a hot dry pan until crisp, about 5 minutes, then turn for 1-2 minutes. Finish with the black pepper.
Salt the cod and leave 10 minutes. Dry well.
Cook in a little butter in a hot pan for 4 minutes, turn, add the rest of the butter and baste for 2-3 minutes until just flaking.
Grill under high heat or over coals for 5-6 minutes per side until the skin blisters and the flesh is opaque at the bone.
Sear in very hot ghee for 1 minute per side, leaving the middle raw.
Fry in foaming butter over high heat for 1-2 minutes per side until pink and curled.
Sear in a little butter in a very hot pan for 90 seconds per side without moving them.
Bring the water and butter to the boil in a wide pot, add the mussels, cover and steam for 4-5 minutes, shaking the pot, until they open.
Salt the sardines and leave 10 minutes.
Fry in hot lard 2-3 minutes per side until crisp.
Cover and steam over gentle heat for 12-15 minutes until just set.
Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 6½ minutes. Cool briefly in cold water and peel.
Make 4 small piles of cheese on a lined tray and bake at 200 °C for 5 minutes until lacy. Lift onto upturned cups to set into bowls.
Bake the eggs in a greased muffin tin with the salt for 8-10 minutes.
Salt the steak and sear in a hot pan for 3-4 minutes per side. Rest while you cook the eggs.
Put the suet and water in a heavy pot over low heat. Let it melt slowly for 2-3 hours, stirring now and then, until the bits are golden and crisp.
Melt the pork fat with the water over very low heat for 2-3 hours, stirring now and then.
Roast the bones at 220 °C for 15 minutes. Scoop out the marrow and let it cool.
Fry in the lard over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Fry in the lard 3-4 minutes per side until golden and flaky.
Sear in a very hot pan 2-3 minutes per side. Add the butter and baste for 1 minute.
Rest 5 minutes; venison is best pink.
Add the broth, cover and simmer gently for 3-3½ hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Slice the beef 3-4 mm thick with the grain. Toss with the salt and leave 1 hour.
Lay the strips on racks over trays. Dry in the oven at 75 °C with the door propped open for 3-4 hours until leathery but still bendable.
Simmer the skin for 1 hour, scrape off any fat underneath and cut into 4 cm pieces.
Dry on a rack at 90 °C for 2 hours until hard.
Spread thinly with the cream cheese, roll up tightly and chill 20 minutes.
Fry in foaming butter over high heat for about 1 minute per side.
Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Mix the pork, onion, egg, flour, milk, salt and pepper into a soft mixture. Rest it 15 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Shape oval patties with a wet spoon and fry them in the butter over medium heat, 5-6 minutes per side, until cooked through. Serve with the potatoes.
Simmer the rice in the milk over low heat, stirring often, for 40 minutes until thick. Stir in the vanilla and sugar and cool completely.
Add the vinegar, sugar, apple, salt and 100 ml water. Cover and cook gently for 50-60 minutes, stirring now and then.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes so the liquid cooks down. Taste for sweet and sour balance.
Soften the leek in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrot and stock and simmer 15 minutes until the potatoes are just tender.
Pour in the cream, add the salmon and salt and simmer gently 5 minutes until the fish flakes. Stir in plenty of dill.
Whisk the sour cream, the other egg, the rest of the sugar and the vanilla and pour over the berries. Bake at 200 °C for 25-30 minutes until set. Cool before slicing.
Whisk the eggs, milk, flour, sugar and salt to a thin batter. Rest 15 minutes.
Pour in the batter and bake 25-30 minutes until puffed and golden. Serve warm with jam or berries.
Simmer the rice in 300 ml water until absorbed, add the milk and half the salt and cook gently 40 minutes to a thick porridge. Cool.

Spread porridge in the middle of each, fold the edges in and pinch them. Bake at 275 °C (or as hot as your oven goes) for 12-15 minutes, brush with butter. Serve with chopped hard-boiled eggs mixed with butter.
Pour in 500 ml water, bring to a boil, cover and simmer very gently for 2-2½ hours until the lamb is tender.
Add the flour, cardamom and milk alternately and whisk smooth, then stir in the butter. Rest 15 minutes.
Shape flat cakes with wet hands and fry in the butter for 3-4 minutes per side. Serve with potatoes and carrots.
Blend the corn with the milk and basil, then cook in the butter with the rest of the salt, stirring, until thick, about 10 minutes.
Spread the corn over the meat, sprinkle with the sugar and bake at 200 °C for 30 minutes until golden.
Slice the onion very thinly and soak it in cold salted water for 10 minutes to soften the bite. Drain.
Add the squash and 500 ml water and simmer 20 minutes until the squash starts to break up.
Add the beans, corn and salt and simmer 10 minutes more. Stir in torn basil.
Simmer the chicken in 1 litre water with half the salt for 30 minutes. Keep the broth.
Blend everything with 400 ml of the broth, pour over the chicken, add the cinnamon and the rest of the salt and simmer 20 minutes until thick. Serve with rice.
Cook, stirring, until the purée is thick enough to pull away from the pan, about 15 minutes. Serve with eggs and tortillas.
Pour boiling water over the cabbage, leave 1 minute and drain well.
Chill at least 2 hours. Keeps a week in the fridge.
Cook the onion in half the palm oil until soft. Add the ginger, tomatoes and whole pepper and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the peas, salt and 200 ml water and simmer 10 minutes. Remove the pepper.
Simmer the chicken, half the onion, ginger and salt in 1.5 litres water for 20 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of the broth and stir it in. Simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the oil rises. Serve with rice balls.
Toss with the ginger, onion, cayenne and salt. Leave 10 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the hot oil in a wok or wide pan, 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and half the ginger, then the tomatoes, salt and spices. Cook over high heat, stirring, until the tomatoes break down and the oil separates, 20 minutes.
Add the chilies and the rest of the ginger, cook 5 minutes and finish with cilantro.
Simmer the lentils in 800 ml water with the turmeric for 20 minutes until soft.
Stir in the spinach and salt and cook 5 minutes.
Fry in hot oil in batches until crisp and golden, 3-4 minutes. Drain and serve with chutney.
Bring the milk to a boil, add the drained rice and simmer on low, stirring often, for 50 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in the sugar and cardamom and cook 5 minutes.
Simmer the lentils with half the onion, the garlic, turmeric and 500 ml water for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk and salt and simmer 5 minutes.
If using dried coconut, soak it in 4 tbsp warm water for 10 minutes.
Add 200 ml water, cover and simmer 25 minutes, then add the coconut milk and simmer uncovered 10 minutes.
Add the beans, turmeric, salt and 3 tbsp water and stir-fry 6-8 minutes until tender-crisp.
Stir in the coconut and cook 1 minute.
Mix the flour with about 160 ml water to a smooth dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll small thin rounds, fill, pleat closed and steam on an oiled rack for 12-15 minutes. Serve with tomato chutney.
Simmer the lentils with the turmeric, ginger and 1 litre water for 25 minutes until soft. Whisk to break up and add the salt.
Pour into the dal, cover for a minute and serve with rice.
Soak the ginger in the lime juice for 10 minutes.
Blend the onion, garlic and ginger and fry the paste in a little oil until golden. Add the turmeric, paprika and chicken and cook 5 minutes.
Add 1 litre water and simmer 20 minutes. Whisk the chickpea flour with a little water and stir in with the coconut milk and fish sauce; simmer 10 minutes.
Fry the paste in the oil with the paprika and turmeric over medium heat until the oil separates, 10 minutes.
Add the pork, soy sauce and 400 ml water, cover and simmer 75 minutes until tender, uncovering at the end to thicken.
Cover and simmer gently 1 hour. Cook the rice and spoon the pork and sauce over it with a halved egg.
Cover and cook 15 minutes, then uncover and reduce until sticky. Stir in the basil.
Marinate the chicken in the soy sauce, rice wine, garlic and half the five spice for 20 minutes.
Toss in the potato starch and fry in hot oil in batches until crisp, 4-5 minutes.
Mix the flour with the hot water to a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest 30 minutes covered.
Fry in a little oil over medium heat 3 minutes per side until crisp and flaky.
Soften the onion and carrot in a little oil, add the beets, tomato paste and vinegar and cook 10 minutes.
Add the stock and potatoes and simmer 15 minutes, then the cabbage for 15 minutes more.
Season, rest 10 minutes and serve with sour cream and dill.
Mix the flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt to a soft dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Roll the dough thin, cut 7 cm rounds, fill and seal. Boil in salted water until they float plus 2 minutes. Serve with the rest of the onion and sour cream.
Brown the lamb in the hot oil in a heavy pot, add the onions and cook until golden, then the carrots, cumin and salt for 10 minutes.
Add water just to cover and simmer 40 minutes.

Spread the rice on top without stirring, add water to 1.5 cm above the rice and push the garlic cloves into it. Cook uncovered until the water is absorbed, then cover tightly and cook on very low heat 25 minutes. Mix before serving.
Add the potatoes and stock and simmer 25 minutes, mashing some potatoes to thicken.
Boil the shrimp for 1-2 minutes until just pink and cool in iced water.
Mix the shrimp, onion with its lime, the tomato mix, the other 2 tomatoes chopped, salt and cilantro. Chill 30 minutes. Serve with popcorn or plantain chips.
Grill 5 minutes on each side for medium-rare, turning once; a thermometer should read 54 °C in the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes on a warm plate, then slice across the grain and season with the pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 °C for 5 minutes. Pat the steak dry, brush with the butter and salt both sides.
Air fry for 5 minutes, turn and air fry 5 minutes more for medium-rare (54 °C inside). Thinner cuts need a minute or two less.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing across the grain.
Pat the steak dry and salt it on both sides 30 minutes ahead if you have time (or just before cooking).
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat until smoking. Cook the steak 3 minutes on the first side without moving it.
Turn it, add the butter and, as it foams, tilt the pan and spoon the butter over the steak for 3 minutes for medium-rare (54 °C inside), longer if you like it more done.
Rest the steak 5 minutes, slice across the grain and pour over the pan butter. Finish with the pepper.
Grill 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, turning once; a thermometer should read 54 °C in the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes on a warm plate, then slice across the grain and season with the pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 °C for 5 minutes. Pat the steak dry, brush with the butter and salt both sides.
Air fry for 4 minutes, turn and air fry 4 minutes more for medium-rare (54 °C inside). Thinner cuts need a minute or two less.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing across the grain.
Pat the steak dry and salt it on both sides 30 minutes ahead if you have time (or just before cooking).
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat until smoking. Cook the steak 3 minutes on the first side without moving it.
Turn it, add the butter and, as it foams, tilt the pan and spoon the butter over the steak for 3 minutes for medium-rare (54 °C inside), longer if you like it more done.
Rest the steak 5 minutes, slice across the grain and pour over the pan butter. Finish with the pepper.
Grill 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, turning once; a thermometer should read 54 °C in the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes on a warm plate, then slice across the grain and season with the pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 °C for 5 minutes. Pat the steak dry, brush with the butter and salt both sides.
Air fry for 4 minutes, turn and air fry 4 minutes more for medium-rare (54 °C inside). Thinner cuts need a minute or two less.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing across the grain.
Pat the steak dry and salt it on both sides 30 minutes ahead if you have time (or just before cooking).
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat until smoking. Cook the steak 2 minutes on the first side without moving it.
Turn it, add the butter and, as it foams, tilt the pan and spoon the butter over the steak for 2 minutes for medium-rare (54 °C inside), longer if you like it more done.
Rest the steak 5 minutes, slice across the grain and pour over the pan butter. Finish with the pepper.
Grill 3 minutes on each side for medium-rare, turning once; a thermometer should read 54 °C in the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes on a warm plate, then slice across the grain and season with the pepper.
Preheat the air fryer to 200 °C for 5 minutes. Pat the steak dry, brush with the butter and salt both sides.
Air fry for 3 minutes, turn and air fry 3 minutes more for medium-rare (54 °C inside). Thinner cuts need a minute or two less.
Rest 5 minutes before slicing across the grain.
Pat the steak dry and salt it on both sides 30 minutes ahead if you have time (or just before cooking).
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat until smoking. Cook the steak 4 minutes on the first side without moving it.
Turn it, add the butter and, as it foams, tilt the pan and spoon the butter over the steak for 4 minutes for medium-rare (54 °C inside), longer if you like it more done.
Rest the steak 5 minutes, slice across the grain and pour over the pan butter. Finish with the pepper.
Grill 5 minutes on each side for medium-rare, turning once; a thermometer should read 54 °C in the thickest part.
